appDescription.message: Quickly and securely zoom videos to fill your browser on most sites. Control the size when fullscreen is too big.

actionDefaultTitle.message:
Click to zoom video on page.
Right-click to change Options

optionsAdvancedFeaturesDescription.message: Some sites lose their playback controls when zoomed. Advanced features allow you to skip and change playback speed.

optionsAdvancedFeaturesHelpLink.message: See the Help ↗ page for more details about how to use advanced features.

optionsWholeDomainLegend.message: Allow more access - whole site by default

optionsWholeDomainLabel.message: May help reduce the number of "rezooms" required to get all permission prompts from chrome.

optionsWholeDomainFeedbackQuestion.message: Is this setting useful for anyone? I'm considering removing it if ends up being more confusing than helpful.

optionsWholeDomainPromptFrom.message:
Changes permissions prompt from:
  "Read and change your data on www.example.com"
to:
  "Read and change all your data on example.com sites"

optionsWholeDomainHelp.message: Can help reduce the number of prompts per new site since you won't get prompted for "www.example.com" and "static.example.com" separately.

optionsWholeDomainQuestion.message: Is the message difference more scary when it says "all your data"?

optionsAllSitesLegend.message: Allow full access to all sites by default

optionsAllSitesLabel.message: If the security prompts annoy you OR Video Maximizer still won't work, then try this setting.

optionsAllSitesWarning.message:
WARNING: It will allow FULL ACCESS to ALL SITES by default.
This access should not be required, but is a fix-all. Once granted and accepted, it silences all further permissions prompting.

Find a site that still doesn't work? Open a GitHub issue ↗.

optionsPlaybackSkippingDescription.message: While Video Maximizer popup controls are displayed, you can use the arrow keys to skip playback. Playback skipping is in viewing times, not video time. For example, 2x playback speed skips twice as far.

optionsPlaybackSkippingHelpLink.message: Read more on the help page

optionsHotkeyDescription.message: To have a hotkey activate VideoMaximizer on page, simply use the built-in Chrome feature. Go to Extensions in Chrome and select "Keyboard shortcuts" from the left. Or navigate directly to chrome://extensions/shortcuts

optionsSpeedControlsLabel.message: Some sites that are already fullscreened in theater mode, so VideoMax won't try to zoom them again. But speed controls could still be nice. Just use main domain part. So for "www.example.com" or "example.uk.co", just supply "example"

optionsAddNewSiteNote.message: Adding a new site? Consider submitting a bug on github to get it added to future releases.

optionsReportProblemsLink.message: Report problems via   GitHub issue ↗

optionsIncludeInfoLabel.message: Include this information in the report:

optionsDisableAdvancedAlert.message:
This will remove the speed controls.

To access this Option page in the future, RIGHT-CLICK on the extension's icon in toolbar and select "options"

optionsAllSitesAlert.message:
Enabling this feature will prompt you ONE last time to grant this extension FULL ACCESS.

You may need to REFRESH the video page before it takes effect.

optionsPromptDomain.message: New domain name to exclude from zooming:

helpFeature1.message: Enhanced Security. Grants access only after you approve once.

helpFeature2.message: NEW Prompt for Advanced UI (for upgrading v2 users)

helpFeature3.message: Arrow keys enable video rewind/forward skipping

helpFeature5.message: Settings to automatically grant extra permissions that reduces security prompts

helpReportingIssuesText.message: Any problems or feature requests can be reported with a new GitHub issue ↗. Chrome's store support does not notify the author when new issues are added.

helpPrompts.message: Prompts for permissions to increase security and maintain your privacy.

helpNoDataCollectionText.message: Privacy and security are a top priorities.

helpWhyPlaybackControlsText.message: Video Maximizer does its best to include the original playback controls when zooming, but some sites may still fail and end up missing them. That's when having some basic playback controls as part of Video Maximizer comes in handy.

helpPlaybackFeatures.message: The feature allows: pause, skip and speed control directly from the extension.

helpSecondPrompt.message: On pages where videos are actually hosted on a different site, it may require a second permissions prompt (e.g. misc sites embedding youtube videos). This appears to be a limitation of the Chrome APIs but hopefully will improve in future versions.

helpSpeedControlsFail.message: If the speed controls fail or the layout isn't centered, then unzoom and rezoom to see if you get another permissions prompt.

helpPermissionsRemembered.message: Permissions are remembered by Chrome and you should not be asked again for the same site.

helpAfterZooming.message: After zooming, clicking the Video Maximizer button shows extra options to control playback speed.

helpWhySpeedControlFailsHeading.message: Why speed control fails on some sites

helpCrossDomainVideos.message: When pages load their videos from a different site (e.g. a youtube video embedded in a non-youtube site), then the speed control feature will not work without permissions to both sites.

helpTryRezooming.message: If this happens, you can try rezooming a couple of times and see if more Access prompts show up. Yes, the multiple promptings can be annoying, but it's just how Chrome works and you will only be asked once per site. If you grant permissions, then you will NOT be prompted again.

helpExtraPermissions.message: If you continue to have access issues or find the prompting annoying there are extra permissions you can try in the Video Maxmizer Options page.

helpAllowAllSites.message: The "Allow access to all sites by default" in the Options will increase this extension's base permissions.

helpPrivacyThoughtsText.message: when granting sites individual permissions, Chrome saves the list of domains with the extension. (See Chrome's Extension page, then click "Details" for the extension.) This list is preserved even if you delete your browsing history. If this is a concern for you, then enabling "Allow access to all sites by default" will grant Video Maximizer access to sites when you activate the extension, but the internal Chrome list will no longer track it.

helpFundamentalIssue.message: The fundamental issue is how the cross-domain-frame-permissions-granting works in Chrome. See Issue #826433 ↗

helpUnzoomFunction.message: The Unzoom function can be accessed by clicking this icon (or the Spacebar after opening)

helpSpeedToggle.message: Clicking the speed-change button a second time toggles it back to normal speed.

helpRelativeSkipTimesDesc.message:
Changing playback speed adjusts how long the skip is.
0.25x playback speed is 1/4th less the skip time.
e.g. 10s skip at 16x playback would skip forward 1m 40s in the video.

helpLengthOfSkipsDesc.message: Can be customized in the Options.

helpTipEscapeDesc.message: Pressing the Escape key on the page UNZOOMS.

helpTipEscapePopupDesc.message: Pressing escape when the Speed Control window is open will close it.

helpNoteSpeedChangingDesc.message: Speed changing will not work on sites hosting videos from other sites without unzooming and rezooming to see if there are additional access prompts. This should only be required once per site, but can be bypassed if you enable the "full access to all sites by default" in Options

helpNoteDisableDesc.message: There is an option to disable the Speed Controls to revert to the behavior of the original Video Maximizer (see Options below)

helpKeyboardShortcutZoomDesc.message: This is built into chrome! Go to chrome://extensions/shortcuts

helpPinningHeading.message: Pinning the extension to the toolbar makes it easier to use.

helpPinningStep1.message: To pin, first click on the Extensions puzzle piece icon

helpNetflixIssueText.message: Skipping the video backwards on netflix causes an error. There's no workaround, so this feature is just disabled for now.

helpSpeedControlsIssueHeading.message: Speed controls don't work on some sites

helpSpeedControlsIssueText1.message: Video Maximizer attempts to use the minimal permissions required to do its job. However, there are still some sites that require more access to work. (The technical reason has to do with embedding iframes that have cross-domain references.)

helpSpeedControlsIssueText2.message: The default settings for Video Maximizer is maximum privacy, but see the Options page for more choices to grant this extension more permissions.

helpDisablingPermissionsHeading.message: Disabling "Allow access to all sites by default" doesn't reset permissions

helpDisablingPermissionsText.message: Another Chrome issue. Video Maximizer removes the extra permissions; however, since they've already been granted, it seems like the extension must be uninstalled and reinstalled to reset it.

helpConstantPromptingText.message: You should only get prompted ONCE per unique site you use Video Maximizer on; however, if this frequency annoys you, then you have the choice to enable the "Allow access to all sites by default" option. You will then get one last prompt and never be bugged again.

helpChangingOptionsStep2.message: Select Option from the dropdown menu.

helpChangingOptionsText.message: You can disable the speed controls and revert the behavior back to the classic toggle.

helpLocalFilesText1.message: You can use Video Maximizer with local video files (like .mp4). Simply drag-and-drop into a browser window to start playing the video. Then click the extension button.

helpLocalFilesText2.message: If you have issues with local files working, you may want to check the extension permissions.

helpLocalFilesStep2.message: Find the VideoMaximizer in the list of extensions.

helpLocalFilesStep4.message: Scroll down until you see the "Allow access to file URLs" and make sure it's enabled.

helpLocalFilesText3.message: You can disable the speed controls and revert the behavior back to the classic toggle.
